Why Does My Dog Have Diarrhea? When to Watch at Home and When to See a Vet

The most common causes of dog diarrhea are minor ones, like a sudden food switch or eating treats or human food. But parasites, viruses, pancreatitis or a swallowed object can also be behind it, so if there's blood, vomiting or your dog is lethargic, it's best to see a vet right away.

Common causes of diarrhea in dogs

CauseWhen to suspect it
Sudden food switchYou changed food overnight. The gut needs time to adjust to a new food.
Treats and human foodYour dog ate a lot of fatty food, milk, or a new treat.
StressSomething changed: a move, travel, grooming, boarding, a new family member.
ParasitesPuppies, or dogs who pick things up and eat them on walks. Giardia, roundworms and others can be the cause.
Viruses (such as parvo)Severe diarrhea and vomiting in a puppy who hasn't finished their vaccines. This can be very dangerous.
PancreatitisVomiting, belly pain and low energy together after eating fatty food.
Foreign objectVomiting, diarrhea and loss of appetite after swallowing a toy, bone, plastic bag or similar.

There are other causes too, such as food allergies, enteritis and medication side effects. Only an exam and tests can tell you the exact cause.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

Signs your dog needs a vet right away

  • Bloody diarrhea, or black, sticky poop
  • Vomiting too, or can't even keep water down
  • Limp and low on energy, or in pain when you touch the belly
  • Diarrhea in a puppy who hasn't finished their vaccines, a senior dog, or a dog with an existing condition
  • Diarrhea that lasts more than a day
  • You think they swallowed something

Puppies and small dogs can get dehydrated quickly, so act sooner with them.

What to try at home for mild diarrhea

If it's just once or twice and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day.

  • Plenty of water: make sure clean water is available at all times.
  • Stop treats and human food: start by cutting out any new treat.
  • Go back to the usual food: if you switched recently, return to the old food, and when you do switch, go slowly using the 7–10 day schedule in How to get healthy, firm dog poop.
  • Keep a log: note how many times your dog went and what the color and texture looked like. Compare them with the dog poop color and texture chart.
  • No human medicine: human anti-diarrhea medicine can be dangerous for dogs. Only use what your vet prescribes.

If yellow diarrhea or gray poop keeps coming, also see why dog poop turns yellow or gray.

Frequently Asked Questions

My dog had diarrhea once. Do I need a vet?

If it's once or twice and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day. If there's blood, vomiting or lethargy, or it lasts more than a day, see a vet.

What's the most common cause of diarrhea in dogs?

Minor causes are common, like a sudden food switch, eating treats or human food, or stress. It can also be parasites, a virus or pancreatitis, so if it keeps going, your dog needs tests.

Should I stop feeding my dog when they have diarrhea?

Fasting your dog for a long time on your own isn't recommended. Puppies and small dogs in particular can develop low blood sugar and dehydration. Ask your vet how to feed them.

Can I give my dog human anti-diarrhea medicine?

Human medicine can be dangerous for dogs. Only use medicine your vet prescribes.

My puppy has diarrhea and is vomiting.

If your puppy hasn't finished their vaccines, it could be a virus such as parvo, so go to the vet right away.
